## Functions

### `createRealmProtectedHeadDiagnostics({ ErrorClass, codePrefix })`

A source-private diagnostic family. Factory-created sibling families cannot forge one another's accepted failures, even when they reuse the error class. The owner keeps this object private; no diagnostic authority enters results.

### `async createRealmProtectedHeadStorage(options)`

Kernel-only transaction substrate shared by closed head-source wrappers. Hooks are fixed implementation functions captured at construction, never request fields. A wrapper owns payload semantics and safe projection; this peer owns scope fencing, exact storage I/O, CAS, and uncertainty recovery. It installs no provider, schema registry, authority grant, or subscription. The view brand validates an already acquired view, not permission to acquire it. Existing public storage-binding exports assume trusted module callers; this helper does not isolate hostile code executing in the same origin.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
